[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions
[原文]
The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds
[原文]
As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

basis.text: For softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, the macro-fibrillation index and the fiber length had a downward trend, and the fines content has an upward trend for the softwood fibers during PFI refining, as can be seen in Figure 1. The macro-fibrillation index and fiber length of softwood fibers changed significantly. However, two parameters of hardwood fibers had no significant variations relative to softwood fibers. It might be because of the lower refining pressure that was applied in hardwood fibers. The macro-fibrillation index characterizes external macro-fibrillation. The results of fiber morphology analysis showed that external fibrillation increased with the refining process. It is consistent with the increasing specific surface area (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource).

针叶木和阔叶木经PFI打浆后，纤维长度均呈下降趋势。 [2]
针叶木的纤维长度和宏观细纤维化指数变化显著，而阔叶木的这两个参数相对针叶木没有显著变化。 [2]
这种差别可能是因为阔叶木打浆时施加的refining pressure较低。 [2]
方法中针叶木和阔叶木的每杆长作用力分别为3.33 N/mm和1.77 N/mm，表明阔叶木受到的打浆作用较弱。 [5]

The trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions
[原文]
The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds
[原文]
As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

queries.rewritten: 针叶木（softwood）与阔叶木（hardwood）打浆后纤维长度变化是否相同？打浆（beating/refining）对针叶木和阔叶木纤维长度的影响差异及其原因是什么？请检索比较两类原料打浆前后纤维长度变化的文献，并核查关于差异机理（如纤维形态、细胞壁结构、木素含量、打浆行为）是否存在冲突证据。

本文认为纸张抗张强度的提高主要来自PFI精炼过程中fibrillation和fines的增加。 [1]
上述结果表明PFI精炼提高了fibrillation（尤其internal fibrillation）、纤维swelling以及纸张的tensile strength，但没有降低纤维的tensile strength。 [1]
零距抗张指数通常用于表征纤维本身的拉伸强度。 [1]
零距抗张结果显示PFI精炼没有降低纤维强度。 [1]
零距抗张强度采用Z-Span 2400装置并按ISO 15361标准测试。 [2]

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

basis.text: In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.

candidate.answer:
本文认为纸张抗张指数的提高主要来自PFI磨浆过程中分丝帚化和细小组分增加，而不是单根纤维强度提高。 [1]
文中指出，纤维润胀（以WRV表征）使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [1]
本文结果表明，PFI磨浆提高了分丝帚化程度（尤其是内部帚化）、纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，但没有伴随纤维抗张强度的下降。 [1]
零距抗张指数通常用于表征纤维本身的抗张强度。 [1]
零距抗张结果显示PFI磨浆没有降低纤维强度，这与Kouko等的报道一致。 [1]
零距抗张强度采用Z-Span 2400 apparatus并依据ISO 15361标准测试。 [2]

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

basis.text: In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. basis.text: In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.

basis.text: In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

FT-IR光谱先以1016 cm−1归一化，并采用Savitzky–Golay算法获得导数曲线/二阶导数谱，以根据归属区域确定各氢键组分的峰位。 [1]
拟合波段为3000–3700 cm−1的羟基吸收带，采用Gaussian函数进行非线性拟合，并在Peakfit 4.12软件中完成。 [1]
该羟基带被解卷积为四个主要谱带，包括O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键、O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键、O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键以及自由OH(2)和OH(6)。 [3]
不同氢键及自由OH的相对含量按对应解卷积谱带的面积比例计算，并以百分比列于表中。 [3]

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

该羟基带被解卷积为四个主要谱带，包括O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键、O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键、O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键以及自由OH(2)和OH(6)。

basis.text: The spectral was normalized at 1016 cm−1 and the derivative curve was obtained by applying the Savitzky–Golay algorithm. The wavenumbers of H-bonding components are taken from second-derivative spectra according to regions that are assigned to various H-bonds. Nonlinear fitting of the FT-IR spectral region from 3000 cm−1 to 3700 cm−1 was carried out with Gaussian function in Peakfit 4.12 software (SeaSolve Software Inc., Framingham, MA, USA). The Pearson correlation coefficients were evaluated between the CI and content of various H-bonds, with a statistically significant p-value of <0.05, while using Spss 25.0 statistics software (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1). [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

In the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.

As to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.

The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1). Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

论文报告PFI打浆后各氢键的H键能量、H键距离以及纤维素多晶型几乎不变。 [1] [2]
但同一研究指出，结晶指数、微晶尺寸以及各种氢键的含量会随打浆变化。 [2]
Table 2显示软木纤维从0 r到16000 r时，O(6)H···O(3′)相对含量由28.23降至23.56，O(3)H···O(5)由28.44升至34.92，O(2)H···O(6)由31.40降至29.38；硬木纤维也发生相应变化。 [3]
正文还给出总体变化：O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键在软木和硬木中分别总体下降16.54%和5.91%，O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键分别总体增加22.78%和8.8%。 [1]
作者将O(6)H···O(3′)含量的下降解释为PFI打浆机械作用导致纤维素分子链断裂，并与内外部纤丝化相关；含量增加则说明既有断裂也有新氢键形成。 [1]
因此，“H键能量和距离基本不变”不等于打浆对氢键网络没有影响；论文把打浆引起的可及性、溶胀和纤丝化等变化与超分子结构和分子间氢键联系起来。 [2]

This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).

As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

claims.text: 论文报告PFI打浆后各氢键的H键能量、H键距离以及纤维素多晶型几乎不变。
但同一研究指出，结晶指数、微晶尺寸以及各种氢键的含量会随打浆变化。
Table 2显示软木纤维从0 r到16000 r时，O(6)H···O(3′)相对含量由28.23降至23.56，O(3)H···O(5)由28.44升至34.92，O(2)H···O(6)由31.40降至29.38；硬木纤维也发生相应变化。
正文还给出总体变化：O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键在软木和硬木中分别总体下降16.54%和5.91%，O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键分别总体增加22.78%和8.8%。
作者将O(6)H···O(3′)含量的下降解释为PFI打浆机械作用导致纤维素分子链断裂，并与内外部纤丝化相关；含量增加则说明既有断裂也有新氢键形成。
因此，“H键能量和距离基本不变”不等于打浆对氢键网络没有影响；论文把打浆引起的可及性、溶胀和纤丝化等变化与超分子结构和分子间氢键联系起来。

论文结果确实支持“氢键能量和距离基本不变”：三种氢键的峰位在打浆全程几乎不变，因此由公式得到的氢键能量和距离不变，纤维素晶型也未变。 [1]
但作者没有据此得出氢键网络无影响；摘要将“晶型、氢键距离和氢键能量几乎不变”与“结晶指数、微晶尺寸和各类氢键含量随打浆变化”并列。 [2]
具体地，O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键总量在软木和硬木中分别降低16.54%和5.91%，O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键分别增加22.78%和8.8%；对O(6)H···O(3′)氢键而言，作者提到既有断裂也有形成。 [1]
表2显示三种氢键和free OH的相对含量随打浆转数变化，例如软木O(6)H···O(3′)从28.23变为23.56，O(3)H···O(5)从28.44变为34.92。 [3]
O(6)H···O(3′)氢键含量与CI-XI趋势相似，软木和硬木的Pearson相关系数分别为0.912和0.889，表明其与结晶区及氢键网络相关。 [5]
因此，打浆对氢键的“能量/距离”影响很小，但对氢键网络的“各类氢键相对含量及断裂/形成”有影响。 [1] [2] [3] [5]

 On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(30)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(30) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

claims.text: 论文结果确实支持“氢键能量和距离基本不变”：三种氢键的峰位在打浆全程几乎不变，因此由公式得到的氢键能量和距离不变，纤维素晶型也未变。
但作者没有据此得出氢键网络无影响；摘要将“晶型、氢键距离和氢键能量几乎不变”与“结晶指数、微晶尺寸和各类氢键含量随打浆变化”并列。
具体地，O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键总量在软木和硬木中分别降低16.54%和5.91%，O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键分别增加22.78%和8.8%；对O(6)H···O(3′)氢键而言，作者提到既有断裂也有形成。
表2显示三种氢键和free OH的相对含量随打浆转数变化，例如软木O(6)H···O(3′)从28.23变为23.56，O(3)H···O(5)从28.44变为34.92。
O(6)H···O(3′)氢键含量与CI-XI趋势相似，软木和硬木的Pearson相关系数分别为0.912和0.889，表明其与结晶区及氢键网络相关。
因此，打浆对氢键的“能量/距离”影响很小，但对氢键网络的“各类氢键相对含量及断裂/形成”有影响。

reference_case.question: 论文说打浆后氢键能量和距离基本不变，那是不是说明打浆对氢键网络基本没影响？
reference_case.reference_answer: 不表示完全不变。本文三类氢键的峰位几乎不变，因此据公式推得能量和距离基本不变；但相对含量仍变化：0到16000转，针叶木分子间氢键由28.23%变为23.56%，阔叶木由26.55%变为24.98%。应区分单类氢键能量/距离与不同组分的相对分布。

The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).

As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds. [原文]
Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

In the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.

As to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.

[原文]
The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

PFI打浆对纤维主要有四种作用：内部细纤维化使纤维壁分层、松散和润湿膨胀，外部细纤维化剥离表面微细纤维但仍附着，剪切作用造成纤维切断，并形成细小纤维。 [2]
这些PFI作用会提高纤维的可及性、润湿膨胀、柔韧性和纤维间结合能力。 [2]
随PFI精磨转数增加，外部细纤维化增强、比表面积增加；打浆度和WRV显著升高，原因是更高细纤维化产生新表面和更多孔隙。 [1]
WRV表征的润湿膨胀使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [1]
PFI精磨过程中细小纤维增加，且软木纤维的湿纸幅强度增加更显著，纤维长度对湿纸幅强度起关键作用。 [1]
zero-span拉伸指数结果表明PFI精磨没有降低纤维强度。 [1]
所给证据未提供纤维长度、细小纤维和WRV对纸页强度贡献的定量比较或排序，因此不能判定哪一个贡献最大。 [1] [2]

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

claims.text: PFI打浆对纤维主要有四种作用：内部细纤维化使纤维壁分层、松散和润湿膨胀，外部细纤维化剥离表面微细纤维但仍附着，剪切作用造成纤维切断，并形成细小纤维。
这些PFI作用会提高纤维的可及性、润湿膨胀、柔韧性和纤维间结合能力。
随PFI精磨转数增加，外部细纤维化增强、比表面积增加；打浆度和WRV显著升高，原因是更高细纤维化产生新表面和更多孔隙。
WRV表征的润湿膨胀使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。
PFI精磨过程中细小纤维增加，且软木纤维的湿纸幅强度增加更显著，纤维长度对湿纸幅强度起关键作用。
zero-span拉伸指数结果表明PFI精磨没有降低纤维强度。
所给证据未提供纤维长度、细小纤维和WRV对纸页强度贡献的定量比较或排序，因此不能判定哪一个贡献最大。

reasons.support_C4: 论文明确说明WRV表征的膨胀提高横向柔顺性并有助于纤维网络结合。
reasons.support_C5: 软木细小纤维含量上升、其湿纸幅强度增幅更大且纤维长度重要均有支持，但细小纤维增加并非明确适用于两类纤维。
reasons.support_C6: 论文直接报告零距抗张指数结果表明PFI精磨没有降低纤维强度。
reasons.support_C7: 论文给出定性解释，但未提供各因素独立贡献的定量比较或排名。

candidate.answer:
PFI打浆对纤维的主要作用包括内部细纤维化（纤维壁分层、松散和润胀）、外部细纤维化（从表面剥离仍附着的微细纤维）、纤维切断和细小纤维生成。 [2]
这些作用会提高纤维的可及性、润胀性、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。 [2]
随PFI转数增加，打浆度和WRV显著上升，文中归因于更高程度的细纤维化产生新的表面和更多孔隙。 [1]
外部细纤维化随打浆进行而增加，并与比表面积增大一致。 [1]
对软木浆，PFI打浆中宏观细纤维化指数和纤维长度下降、细小纤维含量上升；硬木浆的两个参数相对软木浆无显著变化，作者推测与硬木施加较低打浆压力有关。 [1]
WRV表征的润胀增加使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [1]
零-span抗张指数表明PFI打浆未降低纤维强度；整体上PFI提高了细纤维化程度（尤其内部细纤维化）、纤维润胀和纸张抗张强度，而未降低纤维抗张强度。 [1]
文中指出纤维长度对湿纸幅强度起关键作用，软木纤维湿纸幅强度提高更显著也归因于纤维长度。 [1]
就所提供的证据而言，没有给出纤维长度、细小纤维和WRV对最终纸页强度的相对贡献或统计排序，因此不能据此判定三者中哪一个贡献最大。 [1]

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.
